2026-09-06DeltaTok flow — tc128 compose tokenizer · decoder-only finetune on z + sigma·N(0,I), sigma ~ U(0, 0.8) · encoder frozen · BSC 45421190

A noise-tolerant decoder buys the flow −17.6% raymap — by turning the sampler's step count from a liability into an asset.

Ten epochs of RAE's recipe (third_party/RAE/src/stage1/rae.py:74-86) on the decoder half only. MSEToken reproduces to the digit at every step count, so encode() is bit-identical, the flow is untouched and the decoder is the only thing that changed. Best-achievable against best-achievable over the measured 1…20-step sweep — the source decoder peaks at N=2 and degrades after it, the finetuned one falls monotonically to N=20. Bars are the change against the source at matched N (control BSC:45414635).

The flow read — the 1…20-step sweep, before and after the decoder swap

The finetuned curve is monotone in N and passes the source's best by N=4.

The source decoder has an interior optimum at N=2 (raymap 4.60) and gets worse after it. The finetuned decoder falls monotonically all the way to N=20 and has not plateaued. It clears the source's best raymap at N=4 (4.41 vs 4.60) — four steps, not twenty. Every point is measured: BSC:45498382 filled in N = 2, 3, 4, 8, 12.

Best against best, which is the comparison that matters if you may pick N: raymap 3.79 (ft, N=20) against 4.60 (source, N=2) — −17.6%; pointmap 6.61 against 7.27 — −9.1%; depth 3.68 against 3.63 — +1.2%, the source. So the finetuned decoder wins two of three, and already wins both at N=4. Depth is the exception: it is monotonically worse with more steps for both decoders, so depth wants N=1 and the other two want N=20.

Findings — falsifier 2 of the plan's four

Decoder intolerance was binding — at N=20. At N=1 it was not, and that is where the plan aimed.

1
The ladder flattened outright. At σ=0.82 raymap goes 19.09 → 1.67 and pointmap 18.50 → 4.25. The superlinear knee below MSE 0.30 is gone. The 2026-07-19 wall analysis was right that the decoder could not tolerate latent error, and ten epochs of RAE's recipe fixed it.
2
Falsifier 1 fires at N=20: raymap −35.5% at matched N, and the best achievable read improves −17.6% / −9.1%. Its bar was a ≥30% raymap move, and it prescribes exactly what follows — the finetuned decoder becomes the tokenizer every flow read uses, and the 1…20-step sweep is re-read on it.
3
Falsifier 2 fires at N=1, which is where the plan aimed. Predicted raymap 5.03 → ≤3.5; measured 5.93. Against the ladder on the same decoder: MSE 0.6729 of isotropic noise decodes to 3.01 / 4.25 / 1.67, MSE 0.6677 of flow error to 3.68 / 8.29 / 5.93. The 1-step error is structured, and a noise ball does not cover it.
4
The sampler's step count flips sign. The source decoder peaked at N=2 and degraded after it, so steps were a liability; the finetuned decoder falls monotonically to N=20 and clears the source's best by N=4. The known N=20 penalty was partly a decoder artifact. Depth is the exception — it wants N=1 for both.
5
The probe's framing inverts. Before the finetune the flow's error looked 2–4× more benign than isotropic noise of its size; after it, isotropic noise is 3.5× more benign at N=1. Any future noise-probe argument must be made against the tolerant decoder.
Read the frames with this caveat. They show depth and RGB; the headline gain is LossRaymap, which has no panel, and LossDepth is the one metric that worsens with N in the aggregate. Per-scene depth going either way is expected.
Next, from falsifier 2's text — what is left is the N=1 gap. Either the residual sits in the AR rollout (_rollout_from_z, deltatok_shared.py:374, which feeds each decode's output back as x_prev and the finetune never noised), or it is structured in z. The two candidate cycles are a decoder finetune on flow samples rather than Gaussian noise, and x_prev noise.
Adopt the checkpoint. Better at every σ and at N=20, for a 2–4% token-recon cost the flow never sees. It replaces epoch_100 for flow reads; re-read 2026-09-04_flow_bestofk_regressor_null.md on it.
